root_cause.text: TCP sockets allowed unprivileged users to call `SO_ATTACH_FILTER` in `sk_setsockopt()` and attach cBPF filters without a `CAP_NET_ADMIN` check, enabling a side-channel to infer TCP sequence/ack numbers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (sk_is_tcp(sk) && !sockopt_ns_capable(sock_net(sk)->user_ns, CAP_NET_ADMIN)) { ret = -EPERM; break; }` before `copy_bpf_fprog_from_user()`/`sk_attach_filter()`, and the CVE description states this restriction is needed because an unprivileged application could attach a filter to leak TCP sequence/acknowledgment numbers.
